#fasting #autophagy #intermittentfasting 

What FASTING Does to Your Cells That Exercise Can’t

Does fasting do something inside your cells that exercise never will? 🤔 And what does exercise do that no fast can give you? In this video, we go through the real studies to find out, in plain language.

Your cells have a built-in recycling system called autophagy, and it won a Nobel Prize. Many people say only fasting can switch it on. We start by testing that claim, and the answer might surprise you. Then we look at what a long, quiet stretch without food does that a workout can’t hold for long:

We also cover what exercise does that fasting can’t, and where the science is still unsettled. That includes how little of this has been proven in humans and what a 2022 clinical trial found about time-restricted eating.

👍 If this helped you, like the video, subscribe for more science explained simply, and share it with someone who fasts or trains.

#FastingBenefits #CellHealth #Longevity #HealthScience #StemCells #MetabolicHealth #KetoneBodies #FastingVsExercise #HealthyAging #ScienceExplained,

📚 Sources REFERENCES:
 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, Karolinska Institutet, 2016: autophagy discovery and its role in the starvation response
 Nature, 2012: exercise triggers autophagy in the muscle, heart, and liver of mice
 New England Journal of Medicine, 2019: intermittent fasting review, including the switch from sugar to ketones

#healthyaging #musclegrowth #strengthtraining 

💪 Why does lifting weights sometimes produce little muscle growth after 60? The answer may be something missing from your daily nutrition and workout routine!

As we age, our muscles can become less responsive to protein, a process known as anabolic resistance. But that doesn't mean building muscle and improving strength after 60 is impossible!

In this video, we explore the science behind muscle growth, protein intake, and resistance training for older adults. Discover why protein matters, how much older adults may need, and why challenging your muscles with progressive strength training is essential.

#chairworkout #over50fitness #bellyfatworkout 

Over 50? Looking for a gentle way to strengthen your core, hips, and legs while exercising at home? This full seated chair workout is designed to help adults over 50 stay active, improve strength, and support their overall fitness without getting down on the floor!

In this complete follow-along chair workout, every exercise is performed sitting down. No jumping, no floor exercises, and no complicated equipment needed. Just grab a sturdy chair and get ready to move!

🪑 WHAT YOU'LL DO IN THIS WORKOUT:

We'll guide you through gentle warm-ups, seated cardio movements, abdominal exercises, hip-strengthening movements, and a final 90-second workout finisher.

You'll perform exercises such as seated marching, seated punches, knee-to-opposite-elbow, heel taps, seated twists, leg extensions, seated bicycle, knee squeezes, glute squeezes, hip circles, and more.

❤️ Remember, you cannot target fat loss from only your belly or hips. However, consistent physical activity, strength training, daily walking, and healthy eating can support overall fat loss and better health.

Stay until the end for the 90-second seated finisher and a simple weekly workout plan!

Let's get stronger, healthier, and more active together. Don't forget to LIKE, SHARE, and SUBSCRIBE for more senior-friendly workouts and healthy aging tips!

text:
#tendones #musclestrength #strengthtraining 

💪 Can training your tendons make you stronger and more powerful than someone with bigger muscles? The answer might surprise you!

In this video, discover the science behind tendon training and why strength isn't just about building bigger muscles. Your muscles generate force, but your tendons transfer that force to your bones, helping your body move faster, jump higher, and produce explosive power.

🦵 You'll discover how the Achilles tendon works like a biological spring, storing and releasing elastic energy during running, jumping, and sprinting. We'll explore tendon stiffness, force development, muscle-tendon coordination, and why tendons adapt much more slowly than muscles.

🔥 Learn how isometric holds, heavy resistance training, and progressive jumping exercises can help improve tendon strength and stiffness. We'll also explore scientific studies showing how tendon adaptations can improve physical performance.

Your muscles may be the engine, but your tendons are the connection that helps turn muscle force into powerful movement. Don't underestimate the importance of training both!

What Happens to YOUR BRAIN When You Hum for 60 Seconds? In this video, we break down the real science of humming: sinus nitric oxide, the vagus nerve, heart rate variability, and what brain scans and EEG studies have (and haven't) actually shown. 

A simple closed-mouth hum looks harmless, but it sets off some surprising physics and biology. We start at second zero with the sound itself: how your vocal folds make a tone, why one wave of a 130-cycle hum is longer than you are tall, and why your own hum feels like it's inside your skull.

Then we go inside your sinuses. A research team in Stockholm measured nasal nitric oxide during a quiet breath and during a hum, and found about 15 times more gas coming out while humming. We explain why with the same physics as blowing across a bottle: resonance, plug and spring. 🍼

Next comes your nervous system. We look at the vagus nerve, a mostly "listening" nerve that runs through the territory you use to hum, and a small brain-scan pilot study (12 volunteers) in which emotional regions of the brain went quieter during chanted "Om" and not during a control "ssss" sound.

Then your heart: why breathing at roughly six breaths a minute makes your heart rate swing in big, slow waves, what small studies found about humming and heart rate variability, and the honest result that humming looked about as good as plain slow breathing. ❤️

We also cover the EEG research, the attention study, and a quick hype check on claims you may have seen online. At the end, you can hum along with a full 60 seconds. ⏱️

🎯 WHY SHOULD YOU WATCH THIS VIDEO?
✅ Real studies and real numbers, with the limits of each study explained, so you can trust what you learn.
✅ A clear split between what has been measured, what is a reasonable guess, and what is only an internet rumor.

#bloodsugar #healthyaging #walkingforhealth 

What really happens to your blood sugar when you take a gentle 10-minute walk after dinner? In this video we follow your evening meal from the plate into your bloodstream and into your leg muscles. You'll see why sugar peaks 30 to 60 minutes after eating, why your body handles sugar less well in the evening, and how working muscles pull sugar out of the blood without needing insulin. We also look at why this matters more after 50 and 60, when muscle mass and insulin sensitivity both tend to drop.

Why watch: In people with type 2 diabetes, walking for 10 minutes after the evening meal made the rise in blood sugar 22% smaller than one longer walk at another time of day. You'll learn the best time to start, how fast to walk, simple indoor options for bad weather, a seated calf exercise if walking is hard for you, and safety tips if you take blood sugar medication.

If this helped you, please like the video, share it with someone who sits down right after dinner, and subscribe to Longevity Decoded for more simple body science.
